checks.what: samanid-empire 900/12 vassal_end abbasid-caliphate. The Samanid Empire page supports the direction: 'In the spring of 900, Amr clashed with Ismail near Balkh, but was defeated'; 'Ismail was thereafter recognized as the ruler of all of Khorasan and Transoxiana by the caliph. Furthermore, he also received the investiture over Tabaristan, Ray and Isfahan.' So the caliph is the suzerain and the Abbasid-as-Samanid-vassal relation the compiler opened from abbasid-caliphate/ledger/48 (vassal_start branch 'recorded by the vassal (roles reversed)') is wrong. relation_end tries the key ('vassal', samanid, abbasid) first, so the event closes the reversed relation and leaves the 819 Abbasid-over-Samanid tie open to 999. Trial (my stage): 905 Egypt, Syria, Ray and Isfahan circles are Abbasid direct instead of the Samanid cream tint; 985 has no cream Abbasid patch in Khorasan or the Syrian desert; Samanid 911 snap adds 2,879 instead of 2,362 cells and the Abbasid 911 snap removes 2,159 instead of 1,641 (the Khorasan strip goes to the Samanids in 911 instead of staying cream to 999); the 900 record shows no net change from the reversed relation. Small errors I corrected: the region spec was {region: Khorasan} (2,206 cells, about 558,000 km2) while its text names Khorasan, Tabaristan, Ray and Isfahan; set to ledger/48's union (2,519 cells, about 637,000 km2). vassal_end uses the region only to test that it is not landless, so the compile is unchanged (re-trial identical for this entry). Also made the note's quote verbatim. Month 12 is not on the page (it gives spring 900 for Balkh and no month for the investiture): it only places the event after ledger/48, harmless. Residual, not caused by the entry: about 500 Abbasid direct cells in Khorasan/Turkmenistan in 900-910 (before the patch they were drawn in the Samanid tint, also wrong); the 911 Samanid snap clears them.
checks.fix: Region spec set to {union: [Khorasan, Tabaristan, Ray 100 km, Isfahan 100 km]} (the region of abbasid-caliphate/ledger/48) with matching text; note quote made verbatim; reviewer remark appended to the note.
